# Rapier JXL

> JPEG XL encoder for single-file HTML apps, photography tools and agent image workflows. Pure JavaScript, offline
> in browsers, Node and Deno. Lossless, lossy, native precision, HDR, exact alpha, JPEG transcoding and animation. MIT, no runtime
> dependencies. Sizes (gzip): still worker 86,099 bytes, complete worker (adds animation) 153,162, core 22,783.
> Version 5 keeps no compatibility with 4.x callers.

## Choose a Rapier workflow

Rapier is a phone-first Markdown editor for notes, diagrams, drawing and watercolor painting. It runs offline
as one HTML file on Android, Web and Windows.

1. **Work together live.** Connect to `https://mcp.rapier.website/door/mcp`, then call `open`. Use the returned `editor_url` to work with the person and read `rapier://guide` for the tools.
2. **Deliver an offline editor.** Run `npx rapier-html notes.md` to put the document and editor in one HTML file ([rapier-html](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/tree/main/npm/rapier-html)).
3. **Embed in your app.** Install [rapier-embed](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/tree/main/npm/rapier-embed); mount the editor or reader, with your app's agent over WebMCP in the editor.
4. **Keep portable Markdown.** Use [rapier-markdown-kit](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/tree/main/npm/rapier-markdown-kit) for pictures, editable SVG drawings and layout in one `.md` file. Respect [Will/1](https://github.com/jackskip22/will) `keep`, `append` and `edit` regions.
5. **Encode JPEG XL.** Install [rapier-jxl](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-jxl) to encode pixels, photographs and existing JPEGs in JavaScript.
6. **Host the door.** Run [rapier-server](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/tree/main/server) over your own folder or S3-compatible bucket.

## Start encoding

Install with `npm install rapier-jxl`, then import the self-contained core:

```js
import {encode} from 'rapier-jxl/min';
const rgba = new Uint8Array([255, 0, 0, 255]);
const bytes = encode(rgba, 1, 1, {quality: 100});
```

For one offline HTML file, embed the complete `node_modules/rapier-jxl/dist/rapier-jxl.min.mjs` module and import it
through a Blob URL. [Copyable HTML](docs/reference/ARCHITECTURE.md#one-html-file). Keep the exports and MIT notice.

Agent skills: [Single-file apps](skills/rapier-jxl-single-file-app/SKILL.md) · [Photography](skills/rapier-jxl-photography/SKILL.md).

Two self-starting classic workers, both with optional WASM, effort 1–9, Photo, JPEG transcoding and parallel lossless groups:
- `rapier-jxl/rapier/still-worker`: still pictures, byte-identical to the encoder Rapier's page embeds. 86,099 gzip bytes.
- `rapier-jxl/rapier/worker`: the same plus animation and the other format writers; nothing downloads at runtime. 153,162 gzip bytes.

`rapier-jxl/rapier/min` exports `createEncoder()` and `installWorker()` (complete). Pixel defaults: effort 7, quality 90;
`lossless: true` forces quality 100. JPEG uses effort 7. See [the complete API](docs/reference/API.md#complete-rapier-system)
for typed requests, module-worker spawning and Blob URL lifetime.

Choose an entry point:

| Need | Entry point | Call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core pixel encoder | `rapier-jxl` | `encode(rgba, width, height, {quality: 100})` |
| Lossless photos and artwork | `rapier-jxl/effort` | `encode(rgba, width, height, {quality: 100, effort: 6})` |
| Same search with optional WASM | `rapier-jxl/wasm` | Same API; automatic JavaScript fallback |
| Existing JPEG coefficients | `rapier-jxl/jpeg` | `transcode(jpegBytes, {effort: 4})` |
| Lossy photographic pixels | `rapier-jxl/photo` | `encodePhoto(rgba, width, height, {quality: 90, effort: 5})` |
| Explicit transforms, progression and noise | `rapier-jxl/photo-advanced` | `encodePhoto(rgba8, width, height, {progressive: 'spectral', transforms: 'auto'})`; `lfFrames: 1` also supports alpha and custom transforms/tables |
| Original ICC/custom color/tone metadata | `rapier-jxl/icc` | `encodeProfile(rgba, width, height, {icc})`; ordinary `encode` also accepts `icc` |
| Exact graphics with delta palettes | `rapier-jxl/delta-palette` | `encodeDeltaPalette(rgba8, width, height, {paletteMode: 'auto'})` |
| Authored repeated graphics | `rapier-jxl/patches` | `encodePatches(baseRGBA, width, height, {atlas, patches})` |
| Typed planes, extra channels and previews | `rapier-jxl/channels` | `encodeChannels({width, height, color: [r, g, b], extraChannels}, options)` |
| Still layers, crops, blends and references | `rapier-jxl/layers` | `encodeLayers({width, height, layers: [{image}, {image: detail, x, y, blend: 'blend'}]})` |
| Authored XYB curves | `rapier-jxl/splines` | `encodeSplines(rgba8, width, height, {splines: [splineStroke(points, {colorXYB, sigma})]})` |
| PNG16 or scanline OpenEXR | `rapier-jxl/source` | `await readSource(fileBytes)`; pass its samples and options to `encode` |
| A file, bitmap, image data or canvas to a JPEG XL Blob from a page | `rapier-jxl/image` | `await toJXL(file, {worker: './rapier-still-worker.js'})`; a JPEG is carried and rebuilds exactly ([API](docs/reference/API.md#one-call-from-a-page)) |
| Attach or compress Exif/XMP/JUMBF | `rapier-jxl/metadata` | `withMetadata(bytes, fields)`; `await withCompressedMetadata(bytes, fields)` |
| Stream ordered codestream boxes | `rapier-jxl/container` | `containerChunks(bytes)`; `streamContainer(rawChunks, {level})` |
| Deliver progressive pictures sooner | `rapier-jxl/progressive-container` | `withProgressiveContainer(bytes)`; inspect `progressiveContainerPlan(bytes)`; async metadata goes after the image by default |
| Source-grain treatment | `rapier-jxl/noise` | `encodePhoto(rgba8, width, height, {quality: 40, noise: 'auto'})`; bounded quality25–52 sRGB recipe, clean inputs retain ordinary bytes |
| Authored inverse XYB transform | `rapier-jxl/opsin` | `withOpsin(bytes, {inverseMatrix, opsinBiases, quantizationBiases})`; `reset: true` restores defaults |
| Animated JPEG XL from frames (screen recordings, GIFs, video) | `rapier-jxl/animation` | `encodeAnimation({width, height, loops: 0, frames: [{data, duration}]}, {quality: 100, effort: 3})`; duration in ms, loops 0 forever ([API](docs/reference/API.md#animation)) |

Encoding entry points and `rapier-jxl/metadata` have self-contained `/min` builds; `rapier-jxl/min` selects the core.
Import the complete file to access its public export names; minification renames local functions.
Use readable imports when bundling several capabilities so they share code.

Package: `rapier-jxl`. Version: 5.0.0. Install: `npm install rapier-jxl`.
ES modules with no automatic filesystem or network I/O.
Core payload: 56,573 minified bytes; 22,783 gzip bytes.
Runs in browsers, module workers, Node, and Deno. This package encodes JPEG XL and reconstructs JPEGs it carried; it does not include a JPEG XL pixel decoder.

## Inputs and outputs

- Pixels: exactly `width * height * 4` RGBA samples, row-major. `Uint8Array` or `Uint8ClampedArray` for 8-bit; `Uint16Array` for 10/12/16-bit integers or raw binary16; `Float32Array` for binary32.
- Pixel output: `Uint8Array` JPEG XL file bytes; extension `.jxl`, MIME `image/jxl`. Integer inputs up to 12 bits use a bare codestream; 16-bit integers and floats use a container with a level 10 declaration. JPEG transcode returns `{bytes, width, height, orientation}`.
- `quality`: 1–100. Default 100 for core/effort/wasm, 90 for photo. Quality 100 preserves every source sample, including RGB under zero alpha; alpha stays exact at every quality. A smaller exact stream may satisfy a lossy request.
- `effort`: integer 1–9, default 1. The core has no `effort` option. Effort/wasm 1 writes core bytes; higher lossless efforts add candidates and keep only smaller complete streams. Ordinary 8-bit effort 4 adds color-transform search and local palettes; efforts 5–9 learn one predictor/context model per group with prefix/ANS selection, under the ranked color transform from effort 6, with more predictors at 7 and 8 and a second transform at 9. Equal lengths keep the earlier candidate.
- Input arrays stay unmodified; keep them available and unchanged until completion or cancellation.
- Core, effort, photo and JPEG calls are synchronous; the complete Rapier encoder methods are asynchronous. `encodeSteps`, `encodePhotoSteps`, and `transcodeSteps` yield progress in (0,1]; finish iteration before reading `job.bytes`. A yielded 1 is not generator completion. Set `job.hurry = true` and continue to obtain a completed candidate; leaving the loop cancels. Use a worker to keep a page responsive.
- The same input and options produce the same bytes across JavaScript engines, workers, and optional WASM kernels. A byte-limit prune rejects one candidate without hurrying the whole job.

## Precision and color

- Integer `Uint16Array` defaults to 16-bit; set `bitDepth: 10` or `12` for unscaled code values. The encoder rejects out-of-range samples.
- `sampleFormat: 'float16'` declares raw half words in `Uint16Array`; `Float32Array` infers `'float32'`. Floating-point lossless coding retains supplied IEEE words; decoder output formats can canonicalize NaNs.
- `colorSpace`: `'srgb'` (default), `'display-p3'`, or `'rec2020'`. `transferFunction`: `'srgb'`, `'linear'`, `'pq'`, or `'hlg'`; integer default `'srgb'`, float default `'linear'`.
- `intensityTarget`: peak nits; defaults 10000 for PQ, 1000 for HLG, otherwise 255. Stored as binary16.
- `alphaPremultiplied`: boolean, default false. Associated samples remain associated. No color conversion, tone mapping, HDR clipping, or unpremultiplication.
- Native integer effort 2 also prices untransformed RGB; float lossless has no extra effort search. Native lossy reconstructs integer RGB at quantization-bin midpoints or rounds floating-point mantissas, never alpha. [Numeric bounds and decoder qualifications](docs/reference/API.md#native-precision).
- `icc`: complete RGB/GRAY profile bytes, mutually exclusive with other color declarations. Common pixel/worker calls preserve it. `/icc` also accepts custom primaries, white points, gamma, rendering intent and tone metadata. Color fields describe existing samples; no conversion is performed.
- `readSource` returns typed RGBA and encoding options, including PNG `icc` or custom `colorEncoding`. Spread them into `encodeProfile` from `/icc`; ordinary `encode` handles its named-color or ICC cases. PNG16 supports all filters and Adam7. OpenEXR supports single-part uniform HALF/FLOAT RGB or Y scanlines, optional A, NONE/RLE/ZIPS/ZIP. Uses the platform's `DecompressionStream`. [Exact source forms](docs/reference/API.md#reading-png16-and-openexr).

## Exif and XMP

- `withMetadata(jxlBytes, {exif, xmp, jumb})` returns a new `Uint8Array` with standard `Exif` and `xml ` boxes. It wraps a bare codestream when adding metadata and preserves image coding, color encoding, orientation and other boxes.
- `exif`: raw TIFF `Uint8Array`, beginning with `II` or `MM`, without the `Exif\0\0` prefix or JPEG APP1 header. `xmp`: UTF-8 string or `Uint8Array`. Omitted or `undefined` fields retain existing metadata; `null` removes the field.
- Supply metadata separately; the metadata helper does not extract it or convert color. Supply ICC through the encoder's `icc` option. Keep Exif orientation consistent with the encoded image.
- Requested edits reject containers with JPEG reconstruction data (`jbrd`). The output limit, including metadata, is 16 MiB. [Metadata API](docs/reference/API.md#exif-and-xmp).

## Other entry points and contracts

- `jpeg` preserves admitted coefficients, orientation and original JPEG syntax in a standard `jbrd` box. `reconstructJPEG(bytes)` restores this encoder's original JPEG, or returns null without reconstruction data. `JXL_JPEG` means use another JPEG decoder and encode its pixels when appropriate; invalid reconstruction data raises `JXL_RECONSTRUCTION`.
- JPEG `icc: 'preserve'` embeds the original RGB/GRAY profile. Otherwise recognized sRGB/P3 profiles keep their named-color representation and other admitted profiles are embedded exactly. Original JPEG APP2 reconstruction stays exact either way.
- `jpeg-ans` and `photo-ans` expose their corresponding APIs with ANS candidates from effort 2.
- `wasm` exports `configureKernels` and `kernelMode`. Unavailable or blocked WASM falls back to JavaScript. Configure the same imported module before encoding; readable entry points share `rapier-jxl/kernels`.
- `writer` exposes typed format primitives in readable source. `source`, `kernels`, and `writer` have no `/min` entry.
- `treeLearning: 'sampled'` on effort/wasm selects a separate reduced search: shared trees at 2–3, group trees at 4–9; any observed hurry returns effort 1 exactly. Normally omit it to include all candidates.
- Limits: 16 MiB output; 16,384 pixels per side. Core/effort/wasm 24 million pixels, photo 40 million, JPEG 64 million and 16 MiB JPEG input. Optional source reader uses core dimensions.
- Checked encoder errors: `JXL_INPUT`, `JXL_DIMENSIONS`, `JXL_SIZE`, `JXL_MEMORY`, `JXL_JPEG`. Inspect `error.code`. Writer primitives have unchecked preconditions.

[API, options, and errors](docs/reference/API.md) · [Entry points, embedding, and sizes](docs/reference/ARCHITECTURE.md) ·
[Exports and types](package.json) · [Worker example](examples/worker.mjs) ·
[Payload hashes and import graphs](dist/sizes.json) · [Measured comparisons](docs/ENCODER-COMPARISON.md)

Container helpers preserve image bytes and JPEG reconstruction exactly. `withContainer(bytes, {chunkSize: 65536})` collects ordered `jxlp` boxes; `containerChunks` yields them; `streamContainer` accepts raw chunk iterables with backpressure and a truthful `level` (5 or 10). `maxBytes` defaults to 16 MiB, and `signal` cancels. Framing alone does not make the image progressive.

Optional format controls are opt-in and measured separately. All 27 VarDCT strategies and every raw or compact quantization-table mode
are writable; automatic planning currently compares DCT8/16. Progressive HF passes preserve the final coefficients.
LF1 is exact against the XYB route on the measured corpus; deeper levels can change rounding. A useful LF prefix
includes main DC sections. Noise synthesizes authored grain. Delta auto excludes explicit-palette decoder defects.
Planar channels preserve 1–31-bit integers and valid floating words; extra-channel type, precision and scale are
independent. Chrome155 limits total Modular channels to256 and mishandles metadata dimShift with color scale1;
use per-frame extra upsampling for that case. Wide-canvas small previews expose an oxide0.12.6 TOC defect.
Arithmetic patch/layer alpha above1 needs ImageDecoder or createImageBitmap with premultiplyAlpha:'none' in Chrome155.
See the API for exact schemas, browser limits, and measured optional module sizes.

Metadata `jumb` accepts one Uint8Array or an array of JUMBF payloads. `withCompressedMetadata` defaults to `compression: "auto"`, retaining plain boxes unless Brotli is smaller; `"brotli"` requires compression. A bundled portable codec handles browsers without Brotli streams; an explicit `compress` callback overrides it. `readMetadata` returns owned plain payloads and pending compressed entries; `readMetadataAsync` expands them with a 16 MiB default combined limit and optional `decompress` callback.

`rapier-jxl/container-advanced` supplies `inspectContainer`, `reframeContainer`, `containerBoxHeader`,
`frameIndexPayload`/`withFrameIndex`/`readFrameIndex`, and `gainMapPayload`/`withGainMap`/`readGainMap`.
Extended headers preserve exact payloads. Version-1 `fragmentOrder` requires frame-boundary barriers; normalize
to ordered output for oxide0.12.6. Index offsets count from the naked codestream, durations use authored ticks,
and keyframe independence is the caller's responsibility. Gain maps carry supplied ISO21496 metadata and JPEG XL
gain samples with optional alternate color/ICC; they do not create or apply an HDR rendering. See API bounds.
Compact identity/DCT2 and predefined128×256 tables have documented oxide0.12.6 discrepancies; raw alternatives
remain interoperable. LF levels1–4 combine alpha, explicit transforms, compact tables and HF progression.

## Retained plans, exact overlays and offline format operations

Use `createPhotoPlan` from `rapier-jxl/photo-plan` to reuse one transform layout across qualities. Call
`plan.encode(q)` or `plan.encodeTarget(targetBytes, {minQuality, maxQuality, maxProbes})`, then `plan.dispose()`.
The byte search measures complete files and returns the highest tested fitting quality; size is not monotonic,
so do not describe it as a global optimum. Retained typed arrays default to 256 MiB maximum, with transient
encoding memory additional. Eight-bit sRGB-transfer inputs only; no ICC. Alpha remains exact.

Use `encodeHybrid` from `rapier-jxl/hybrid` for an exact text or graphic rectangle over a YCbCr photograph.
Explicit `regions` expand to 8×8 blocks and retain original RGBA there. Automatic regions keep only a smaller
complete candidate, but analysis can cost several ordinary encodes and does not recognize every text shape.
Quality 100 stays exact. Use authored regions when exactness is required.

Use `withDeliveryOrder(bytes, {region, strategy: 'region-first'})` from `rapier-jxl/delivery` to place selected
groups before other groups. `deliveryLayout` reports section geometry and offsets; `normalizeDelivery` restores
ordinary order for the layer/animation/progressive-container readers. It changes delivery order, not pixels.
Actual TOC changes refuse JPEG reconstruction. The parser accepts its authored prefix permutation syntax.

The complete offline worker includes every format writer. Call `encoder.format({action, ...input, options},
{signal, progress})`, or post `{id, operation: 'format', input, progress: true}`. Byte results use `bytes`;
structured results use `result`. `photoPlan` shares one plan across up to 32 qualities and one optional byte target,
then disposes it; their total output must fit 16 MiB. See the API's action table and declarations.

Metadata has a portable Brotli fallback when browser Brotli streams are absent. `compressBrotli` and
`decompressBrotli` from `rapier-jxl/brotli` are also callable directly. The portable reader supports the writer's
own form, not every external Brotli stream. Preserve unknown compressed payloads with `readMetadata`, or supply
a full bounded decoder for expansion. The complete worker always uses the portable codec for repeatable bytes.
